doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Recording with Rick Fay and nerves in the studio
summary: On Rick Fay's Arbors album with Dan Barrett, Marty Grosz and Hal Smith, he was nervous then, and has since relaxed about perfection.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah. You have to think about the context that you’re in. This particular album was more arranged than some of the — well here we go with words again — classic or whatever. Were these Rick Fay’s arrangements?

Rick Fay is the leader on this. It’s called “This is Where I Came In” right? Arbors Records? Dan Barrett was on there and I think that was Dan Barrett’s arrangement, which was taken largely from one of Bix Beiderbecke’s versions of that song. And he did a lot of arrangements on that album. I think Marty Grosz did do some arrangements on that
album as well. A lot of those guys are here — Marty Grosz, Dan Barrett, Hal Smith is here.

A little bit, yeah, yeah. In a way it was really my second recording session. The other one came out later so I say that this was my first CD because it came out first. Yeah, I mean I was playing with all these top guys. I mean everybody on that album was tops. And I was relatively new to playing with guys of that caliber. After moving to New York I started meeting guys like Dan Barrett, who introduced me to some of these other guys. It was a thrill. It was exciting. I was more uptight then about like wanting everything to be perfect, and worrying about it more than I do now, after having done several recordings. You realize if you worry too much about that you can drive yourself crazy. I’d play the tapes back and I’d get down on myself for everything that wasn’t exactly the way I intended it to be. Now I listen back to it and you know, I forgot what I intended to play, so you know if it came out okay, fine.
Right. Not that it’s not as important to me that it comes out right, but I just used to really drive myself crazy about it.
